COMPUTER SYSTEM SET UP, FILE MANAGEMENT AND NETWORKING
Your school has received the following computer hardware components for use in the
computer laboratory:
 (a) System unit
 (b) Monitor
 (c) Keyboard
 (d) Mouse
 (e) Power cables
 (f) Data cables
As Computer Studies learners, you are required to set up the computers, configure
selected system settings and connect them to a network by performing Task 1, Task
2, Task 3 and Task 4.
Task 1: Setting up a computer system (6 Marks)
Set up a computer by performing the following tasks in turns:
1. Correctly connect all computer hardware components provided.
2. Visit other groups workstations, observe their setups and provide feedback based on
 your observations.
3. Boot the computer and verify that all components are functioning properly.
Task 2: Using an Operating System (14 Marks)
Use the operating system installed in the computer to perform the following tasks in
turns:
1. Create a folder on the desktop. Name it 2026 CS SBA Project.
2. (a) Configure the following system settings:
 (i) Date
 (ii) Language
 (b) Take a screenshot of the settings applied and save it as System Settings in the
 folder created.
3. (a) Open the computer system information and identify the following details:
 (i) Name of the operating system installed.
 (ii) Operating system type.
 (iii) RAM size.
 (iv) Processor type.
 (b) Take a screenshot of the system information and save it as System Information
 in the folder created.
4. (a) Open the task manager and identify information about CPU and memory usage.
 (b) Take a screenshot of the task manager and save it as Task Manager in the folder
 created.
5. Schedule a backup on the computer you are using.
Task 3: Saving and Retrieving Data (10 Marks)
 1. Open a word processing productivity tool and perform the following tasks in turns:
 (a) Create a blank document and save it as Operating System in the folder created
 in Task 2.
 (b) Insert the three screenshots saved in Task 2 into the document.
 (c) Save the changes made to the document.
 2. Retrieve the document created in number 1 and perform the following tasks in turns:
 (a) Take turns to explain the procedure followed to generate each screenshot as your
 peer types each procedure in the retrieved document.
 (b) On the first page of the document, insert the names and assessment numbers of
 each group member.
 (c) Save the document as New Operating System in the folder created in Task 2.
 (d) Shut down the computer.
Task 4: Connecting a computer to a network and sharing data (10 Marks)
Establish a computer network by carrying out the following tasks in turns:
1. Connect the computer set up in Task 1 to a computer network using wired or wireless
 technology.
2. Verify the network connection to ensure that the computer is successfully connected
 to the network.
3. Create a folder named Network Files on the computer.
4. Copy the folder, 2026 CS SBA Project, created in Task 2 into the Network Files
 folder.
5. Share the Network Files folder over the network and set appropriate access
 permissions.
6. Allow other groups to access and open the files in the shared folder from their
 computers.

INSTRUCTIONS TO THE TEACHER
1.0 Computer hardware requirements
 Ensure the following devices required for this practical are available, functional and
 ready for use by learners:
 1.1 System units
 1.2 Monitors
 1.3 Keyboards
 1.4 Mouse
 1.5 Power cables
 1.6 Data cables
 1.7 Ethernet cables or Wi‑Fi router
2.0 Power supply
 Ensure a reliable, stable power supply to prevent interruptions during the practical
 assessment.
3.0 Safety precautions
 Guide learners to observe the following safety precautions when undertaking the
 practical assessment:
 3.1 Ensure the computer is switched off and unplugged from the power source
 before connecting or disconnecting any hardware components.
 3.2 Ensure all cables are connected correctly and securely.
 3.3 Avoid overloading power sockets.
 3.4 Avoid forcing hardware components into ports.
 3.5 Avoid changing critical system settings unless instructed as this may affect the
 proper functioning of the computer.
4.0 Practical assessment instructions
 4.1 This practical consists of FOUR tasks, Task 1, Task 2, Task 3 and Task 4.
 4.2 The practical duration is THREE HOURS. Encourage learners to complete the
 practical within the stipulated time.
5.0 Group formation
 The tasks should be performed in groups of up to five learners. Ensure a balanced
 distribution of learners in each group by:
 5.1 forming mixed ability groups that take into account learners different levels of
 ability;
 5.2 distributing learners skills and strengths evenly across all groups;
 5.3 ensuring gender balance within each group;
 5.4 monitoring group interactions and making adjustments where necessary to
 support effective collaboration;
 5.5 assigning clear roles within each group such as a group leader and a secretary
 to promote responsibility and teamwork;
 5.6 encouraging learners to work collaboratively.
6.0 Administration of the practical assessment
 6.1 Verify that all devices provided to the learners are working correctly.
 6.2 Test the functionality of all the software required before the assessment.
 6.3 Disable unauthorised applications and restrict access to unnecessary files or
 programs.
 6.4 Create or provide user accounts with appropriate permissions for learners.
 6.5 Set up file storage locations for saving learners’work.
 6.6 Disable internet access for tasks that do not require it or restrict access to
 approved resources only.
 6.7 Ensure fairness by giving all learners equal time, instructions and conditions
 for completing the tasks.
 6.8 Ensure each group clearly labels files for each task.
 6.9 Collect and store learners’ work electronically for assessment and scoring.
 6.10 Ensure the e-portfolio includes all required evidence such as documents and
 screenshots.
 6.11 Maintain secure storage of e-portfolios to protect against tampering or loss.
7.0 Scoring the assessment tasks
 Ensure that the scoring of each task is objective, consistent and based on the
 provided scoring guide. To achieve this:
 7.1 use the scoring guide provided to assess the learners performance on the
 tasks;
 7.2 adhere to the criteria as outlined for each task;
 7.3 use clear evidence of each task and award scores based only on observable
 outcomes;
 7.4 assess each criteria independently and score each task step separately to
 avoid bias;
 7.5 standardise marking where two or more teachers are involved. agree on
 scoring interpretations before assessment;
 7.6 enter the scores for individual learners in the score sheet provided.
8.0 Maintaining the e-portfolio
 8.1 Ensure all learner e-portfolios are securely stored in a designated digital
 storage such as flash disks, CD/DVDs, hard disks, a school server or an
 approved cloud platform.
 8.2 Perform regular backups to prevent loss of data.
 8.3 Restrict access to the e-portfolios to authorised persons only.
 8.4 Retain the e-portfolios for one year for verification.
 8.5 Do not make alterations to submitted work after assessment.
 8.6 At the end of the retention period, archive the e-portfolios to support future
 learning and serve as reference materials.
